title: Periodic Table: The First 20 Elements
description: Learn the symbols, names, and atomic numbers of elements 1 through 20, each with one fact to help it stick.
subject: science

cards.definition: Hydrogen, atomic number 1. The lightest element and the most abundant one in the universe.
Helium, atomic number 2. A noble gas lighter than air, used to fill balloons.
Lithium, atomic number 3. The lightest metal, widely used in rechargeable batteries.
Beryllium, atomic number 4. A light, stiff alkaline earth metal used in aerospace parts and X-ray windows.
Boron, atomic number 5. A metalloid used to make heat-resistant borosilicate glass.
Carbon, atomic number 6. The backbone of organic molecules. Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon.
Nitrogen, atomic number 7. Makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.
Oxygen, atomic number 8. Makes up about 21% of the air and is needed for cellular respiration.
Fluorine, atomic number 9. The most electronegative element. Its compounds, fluorides, are added to toothpaste.
Neon, atomic number 10. A noble gas that glows reddish-orange in electric signs.
Sodium, atomic number 11. A soft, reactive alkali metal that combines with chlorine to form table salt.
Magnesium, atomic number 12. An alkaline earth metal that burns with a brilliant white flame.
Aluminum, atomic number 13. The most abundant metal in Earth's crust; light and resistant to corrosion.
Silicon, atomic number 14. A metalloid used in computer chips and the second most abundant element in Earth's crust.
Phosphorus, atomic number 15. Part of the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA and of the energy molecule ATP.
Sulfur, atomic number 16. A yellow nonmetal. Its compound hydrogen sulfide smells like rotten eggs.
Chlorine, atomic number 17. A toxic yellow-green halogen gas used to disinfect drinking water and pools.
Argon, atomic number 18. A noble gas that makes up nearly 1% of Earth's atmosphere.
Potassium, atomic number 19. A reactive alkali metal essential for nerve and muscle function. Its symbol comes from the Latin kalium.
Calcium, atomic number 20. An alkaline earth metal and the main mineral in bones and teeth.
